CHOICE FORMS

I. Choosing Single Elements

1. $C(\infty ,\,\infty )$: The Axiom of Choice: Every set of non-empty sets has a choice function.

5. $C(\aleph _{0},\,\aleph _{0},\,\mathbb{R})$: Every denumerable set of non-empty denumerable subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ has a choice function. Sageev [1975].

8. $C(\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: Every denumerable family of non-empty sets has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918].

[8 M] Form 131+ form 32. Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

10. $C(\aleph _{0},\,<\aleph _{0})$: Every denumerable family of non-empty finite sets has a choice function.

[14 Y] Form 99+ Form 62. Note 33.

[14 BS] Every bounded distributive lattice has a prime ideal choice function. Morillon [1988], [1985] and note 71.

[14 BT] If $(A_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of bounded, distributive, $\vee$-compact lattices and if $(J_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family such that for all $i\in I,\,J_{i}$ is a proper ideal in $A_{i}$ then there is a family $(P_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that for all $i\in I,\,P_{i}$ is a prime principal ideal in $A_{i}$ containing $J_{i}$. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

[14 BU] If $(A_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of distributive non trivial bounded lattices then there is a family $(f_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that each $f_{i}$ is a prime ideal choice function on $A_{i}$. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

[14 BW] For every set $E$ there is an ultrafilter choice function on $E$. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

[14 BX] If $(E_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of sets and $(F_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family such that for each $i,\,F_{i}$ is a filter in $\mathcal{P}(E_{i})$, then there is a family $(U_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that for each $i\in I,\,U_{i}$ is an ultrafilter in $\mathcal{P}(E_{i})$ containing $F_{i}$. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

16. $C(\aleph _{0},\,\leq 2^{\aleph _{0}})$: Every denumerable collection of non-empty sets each with power $\leq 2^{\aleph _{0}}$ has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918].

24. $C(\aleph _{0},2^{(2^{\aleph _{0}})})$: Every denumerable collection of non-empty sets each with power $2^{(2^{\aleph _{0}})}$ has a choice function. G. Moore [1982].

28. $C(\aleph _{0},2^{\aleph _{0}})$: Every denumerable collection of non-empty sets each with power $2^{\aleph _{0}}$ has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918].

32. $C(\aleph _{0},\,\leq \aleph _{0})$: Every denumerable set of non-empty countable sets has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918].

[32 A] $C(\aleph _{0},\,\aleph _{0})$. Every denumerable set of denumerable sets has a choice function.

33($n$). If $n\in \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(LO,\,n)$: Every linearly ordered set of $n$ element sets has a choice function. Truss [1973a].

39. $C(\aleph _{1},\,\infty )$: Every set $A$ of non-empty sets such that $|A|=\aleph _{1}$ has a choice function. Sierpiński [1918], G. Moore [1982] p. 202.

40. $C(WO,\,\infty )$: Every well orderable set of non-empty sets has a choice function. G. Moore [1982] p 325.

45($n$). If $n\in \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(\infty ,\,n)$: Every set of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].

46 ($K$). If $K$ is a finite subset of $\omega -\{0,\,1\},\,C(\infty ,\,K)$: For every $n\in K$, every set of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].

47($n$). If $n\in \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(WO,\,n)$: Every well ordered collection of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].

48($K$). If $K$ is a finite subset of $\omega -\{0,\,1\},\,C(WO,\,K)$: For every $n\in K,\,C(WO,\,n)$. Mostowski [1945], Truss [1973a].

60. $C(\infty ,\,WO)$: Every set of non-empty, well orderable sets has a choice function. Jech [1973b], G. Moore [1982] p 125.

[60 A] $(\forall \alpha )C(\infty ,\,\aleph _{\alpha })$: For every ordinal $\alpha$, every family of sets each with power $\aleph _{\alpha }$ has a choice function.

61. $(\forall n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2)(C(\infty ,\,n))$: For each $n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2$, every set of $n$ element sets has a choice function. Levy [1962].

62. $C(\infty ,\,<\aleph _{0})$: Every set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function.

[79 A] $C(\infty ,\,\infty ,\,\mathbb{R})$: Every set whose elements are non-empty subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ has a choice function. Schechter [1996a].

80. $C(\aleph _{0},2)$: Every denumerable set of pairs has a choice function. Mostowski [1948].

85. $C(\infty ,\,\aleph _{0})$: Every family of denumerable sets has a choice function. Jech [1973b] p 115 prob 7.13.

[85 A] $C(\infty ,\,\leq \aleph _{0})$: Every family of non-empty countable sets has a choice function.

86($\alpha$). $C(\aleph _{\alpha },\,\infty )$: If $X$ is a set of non-empty sets such that $|X|=\aleph _{\alpha }$, then $X$ has a choice function. Levy [1964].

88. $C(\infty ,\,2)$: Every family of pairs has a choice function.

94. $C(\aleph _{0},\,\infty ,\,\mathbb{R})$: Every denumerable family of non-empty sets of reals has a choice function. Jech [1973b] p 148 prob 10.1.

[111 A] $C(WO,\,2)$: Every well ordered family of 2-element sets has a choice function.

[118 I] Every linearly ordered set of linear orders, each of which is non-empty and conditionally complete, has a choice function. Morillon [1988], van Douwen [1985], and note 71.

[118 M] If $(X,\,\leq )$ is a linear order, then the family $\{A(a,\,b):a,\,b\in X\wedge a<b\}$ has a choice function. ($A(a,\,b)$ denotes the set of continuous, order preserving functions from $X$ into $[0,1]$ such that $f(a)=0$ and $f(b)=1$.) Morillon [1988] and note 71.

[118 N] If $(X,\,\leq )$ is a linear order then the family $\{A^{\prime }(a,\,b):a,\,b\in X\wedge a<b\}$ has a choice function. ($A^{\prime }(a, b)$ denotes the set of continuous functions from $X$ into $[0,1]$ such that $f(a)=0$ and $f(b)=1.)$ Morillon [1988] and note 71.

[118 S] If $(X,\,\leq )$ is a complete linear order then there is a choice function $\ast$ for the family of non-empty open intervals of $X$ such that if $a,\,b,\,c\in X$ and either $(a,\,b)\neq \emptyset$ or $(b,\, c)\neq \emptyset$ then $\ast ((a,\,c))\in \{\ast ((a,\,b)), \ast ((b,\,c)), b,\,b^{+}\}$ (where $b^{+}$ is the successor of $b$ if it exists and $b$ otherwise). Morillon [1987] and note 71.

[118 T] Every complete linear order has an increasing choice function. Morillon [1987] and note 71.

119. $C(\aleph _{0},{\text{uniformly orderable with order type of the integers}})$: Suppose $\{A_{i}: i\in \omega \}$ is a set and there is a function $f$ such that for each $i\in \omega ,\,f(i)$ is an ordering of $A_{i}$ of type $\omega ^{\ast }+\omega$ (the usual ordering of the integers), then $\{A_{i}:i\in \omega \}$ has a choice function. van Douwen [1985].

120($K$). If $K\subseteq \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(LO,\,K)$: Every linearly ordered set of non-empty sets each of whose cardinality is in $K$ has a choice function. Truss [1973a].

121. $C(LO,\,<\aleph _{0})$: Every linearly ordered set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function. Truss [1973a].

122. $C(WO,\,<\aleph _{0})$: Every well ordered set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function. Truss [1973a].

165. $C(WO,\,WO)$: Every well ordered family of non-empty, well orderable sets has a choice function.

181. $C(2^{\aleph _{0}},\,\infty )$: Every set $X$ of non-empty sets such that $|X|=2^{\aleph _{0}}$ has a choice function. Freyd [1980].

194. $C(\varPi _{2}^{1})$ or $AC(\varPi _{2}^{1})$: If $P\in \omega \times ^{\omega }\omega ,\,P$ has domain $\omega$, and $P$ is in $\varPi _{2}^{1}$, then there is a sequence of elements $\langle x_{k}: k\in \omega \rangle$ of $^{\omega }\omega$ with $\langle k,\,x_{k}\rangle \in P$ for all $k\in \omega$. Kanovei [1979] and note 61.

202. $C(LO,\,\infty )$: Every linearly ordered family of non-empty sets has a choice function. Truss [1978].

203. $C(\mathrm{disjoint},\subseteq \mathbb{R})$: Every partition of $\mathcal{P}(\omega )$ into non-empty subsets has a choice function. Truss [1978].

212. $C(2^{\aleph _{0}},\,\subseteq \mathbb{R})$: If $R$ is a relation on $\mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x\in \mathbb{R}$, there is a $y\in \mathbb{R}$ such that $x\,R\,y$, then there is a function $f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x\in \mathbb{R},\,x\,R\,f(x)$. Mathias [1977a].

213. $C(\infty ,\,\aleph _{1})$: If $(\forall y\in X)(|y|=\aleph _{1})$ then $X$ has a choice function. Pincus [1977a].

250. $(\forall n\in \omega \,-\{0,1\})(C(WO,\,n))$: For every natural number $n\geq 2$, every well ordered family of $n$ element sets has a choice function. Truss [1975].

288($n$). If $n\in \omega \,-\{0,1\},\,C(\aleph _{0},\,n)$: Every denumerable set of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Wiśniewski [1972].

[308 $\mathbf{B}(p)$] If $p$ is a prime and if $Y$ is a set of non-empty finite sets such that $(\forall y\in Y)(\mathrm{gcd}(|y|,\,p)=1)$, then $Y$ has a choice function. (This is similar to form 46$(K)$, but in 46$(K)$ the set $K$ is required to be finite.) Howard/Yorke [1987].

[308 $\mathbf{C}(p)$] If $p$ is a prime and if $Y$ is a set of non-empty finite sets such that $(\forall y\in Y)(|y|\equiv 1\mod \,p)$, then $Y$ has a choice function. (This is similar to form 46$(K)$, but in 46$(K)$ the set $K$ is required to be finite.) Howard/Yorke [1987].

[374 $\mathbf{A}(n)$] For each $i,\,2\leq i\leq n\in \omega -\{0,1\},\,C(\aleph _{0},\,i)$: Every denumerable set of $i$-element sets has a choice function.

II. Dependent Choice

[$\boldsymbol{0}$ X] $DC(\boldsymbol{\Sigma }_{2}^{1})$: If $P\subseteq {^{\omega }\omega } \times {^{\omega }\omega }$ and $P$ has domain ${^{\omega }\omega },\,P\in \boldsymbol{\Sigma }_{2}^{1}$, then for any $y\in {^{\omega }\omega }$ there is a sequence $\langle x_{k}: k\in \omega \rangle$ of elements of $^{\omega }\omega$ with $x_{0}=y$ and $\langle x_{k},\,x_{k+1}\rangle \in P$ for all $k\in \omega$. Kanovei [1979] and note 61.

[1 F] For all ordinals $\alpha ,\,DC(\aleph _{\alpha })$: Given a relation $R$ such that for every subset $Y$ of a set $X$ with $|Y|<\aleph _{\alpha }$, there is an $x\in X$ with $YR\,x$, then there is a function $f:\aleph _{\alpha }\rightarrow X$ such that $\forall \beta <\aleph _{\alpha },\, \{f(\gamma ):\gamma <\beta \}\,R\,f(\beta )$.) Levy [1964] and note 133.

43. $DC(\omega )$ ($DC$), Principle of Dependent Choices: If $S$ is a relation on a non-empty set $A$ and $(\forall x\in A)(\exists y\in A)(xSy)$ then there is a sequence $a(0), a(1), a(2),\ldots$ of elements of $A$ such that $(\forall n\in \omega ) (a(n)\,S\,a(n+1))$. Tarski [1948] p 96, Levy [1964] p 136 and note 54.

[43 S] If $S$ is a relation on $A$ such that $(\forall x\in A)(\exists y\in A)(x\,S\,y)$ and $x_{0}$ is any element of $\mathrm{A}$, then there is a sequence $a(1),a(2),\ldots$ of elements of $A$ such that $a(n)\,S\,a(n+1)$ for all $n\in \omega$ and such that $a(0)=x_{0}$. Notes 101 and 54.

44. $DC(\aleph _{1})$: Given a relation $R$ such that for every subset $Y$ of a set $X$ with $|Y|<\aleph _{1}$ there is an $x\in X$ with $Y\,R\,x$, then there is a function $f:\aleph _{1}\rightarrow X$ such that $(\forall \beta <\aleph _{1})(\{f(\gamma ):\gamma <b\}\,R\,f(\beta ))$. Levy [1964].

87($\alpha$). $DC(\aleph _{\alpha })$: Given a relation $R$ such that for every subset $Y$ of a set $X$ with $|Y|<\aleph _{\alpha }$, there is an $x\in X$ with $Y\,R\,x$ then there is a function $f:\aleph _{\alpha }\rightarrow X$ such that $(\forall \beta <\aleph _{\alpha })\{f(\gamma ):\gamma <\beta \}\,R\,f(\beta )$. Levy [1964].

[106 A] $DMC$: Dependent Multiple Choice: Every tree in which every element has at least one immediate successor has a subtree whose levels are finite and in which every element has at least one immediate successor. Blass [1979], Brunner [1983c], Fossy/Morillon [1995] and note 21.

[106 B] Weak $\mathrm{DC}$: If $R$ is a binary relation on a non-empty set $E$ such that $(\forall x\in E)(\exists y\in E)(x\,R\,y)$, then there is a sequence $\langle F_{n}\rangle _{n\in \omega }$, of non-empty finite subsets of $E$ such that ($\forall n\in \omega ) (\forall x\in F_{n})(\exists y\in F_{n+1})(x\,R\,y)$. (This statement remains equivalent to form 106 if we replace “binary relation” by “transitive binary relation”.) Fossy/Morillon [1995].

211. $DCR$: Dependent choice for relations on $\mathbb{R}$: If $R\subseteq \mathbb{R}\ \times \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $(\forall x\in \mathbb{R})(\exists y\in \mathbb{R})(x\,R\,y)$ then there is a sequence $\langle x(n): n\in \omega \rangle$ of real numbers such that $(\forall n\in \omega )(x(n)\,R\,x(n+1))$. Mathias [1977a].

III. Multiple Choice and Kinna-Wagner Principles

[1 E] $K(0)$: For every set $S$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a one to one function $f:S\rightarrow \alpha$. (See form 81$(n)$).

[1 BY] If $x$ is a set of sets of cardinality at least 2, then there exists a function $f$ such that for each $u\in x,\,f(u)$ is a finite, non-empty, proper subset of $u$. (Form [1 BY] implies [62 E] $(KW(\infty ,\,<\aleph _{0})$) and 67 (MC) and $62+67\rightarrow \mathrm{AC}$.) Blass [1979].

[1 CC] $PC(\aleph _{0},\,\mathrm{odd},\,\infty ) +MC_{\omega ^{+}}$. $PC(\aleph _{0},\,\mathrm{odd},\,\infty )$ is “Every denumerable family of odd sized (finite) sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function.” and $MC_{\omega ^{+}}$ is “For every natural number $n\geq 1$ and for every set of non-empty sets, there is a function $f$ such that for each $u\in x,\,f(u)$ is a non-empty finite subset of $u$ such that $|f(u)|$ and $n$ are relatively prime.” Note 133.

[8 M] Form 131+ form 32. Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

[8 O] $DUCCC\ +$ form 131. $DUCCC$ is “If $X$ is a denumerable family of disjoint topological spaces each having the ccc property, then the disjoint union of the spaces in $X$ has the ccc property.” ($Y$ has the ccc property if every collection of disjoint open sets is countable.) Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

[8 P] $DUSS\ +$ form 131. $DUSS$ is “The disjoint union of a denumerable family of separable topological spaces is separable.” Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

[8 Q] $DUSC\ +$ form 131. $DUSC$ is “The disjoint union of a denumerable family of second countable topological spaces is second countable.” Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

[8 R] $SCDUL\ +$ form 131. $SCDUL$ is “The denumerable disjoint union of second countable spaces is Lindelöf.” Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

[14 AT] Assume $D$ and $E$ are sets and for all $d\in D,\,d$ is finite. Suppose that for every finite $F\subseteq D$, there is an $S$ such that $(\forall f\in F)(f\cap \,S\in E)$. Then there is an $S$ such that $(\forall d\in D)(d\cap \,S\in E)$. van Benthem [1975].

15. $KW(\infty ,\,\infty )$ (KW), The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle: For every set $M$ there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in M$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form $81(n)$). Kinna/Wagner [1955].

[62 E] $KW(\infty ,\,<\aleph _{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for families of finite sets: For every set $M$ of finite sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in M$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. Note 70.

67. $MC(\infty ,\,\infty )$ (MC), The Axiom of Multiple Choice: For every set $M$ of non-empty sets there is a function $f$ such that ($\forall x\in M)(\emptyset \neq f(x)\subseteq x$ and $f(x)$ is finite).

76. $MC_{\omega }(\infty ,\,\infty )\ (\omega {\text{-}}\mathrm{MC})$: For every family $X$ of pairwise disjoint non-empty sets, there is a function $f$ such that for each $x\in X,\,\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is a non-empty countable subset of $x$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b].

[106 A] $DMC$: Dependent Multiple Choice: Every tree in which every element has at least one immediate successor has a subtree whose levels are finite and in which every element has at least one immediate successor. Blass [1979], Brunner [1983c], Fossy/Morillon [1995] and note 21.

[106 D] For every compact $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ space $(X,\,T)$ and every family $D=\{D_{i}:i\in \omega \}$ of dense open sets of $X$ there is a regular filter base $\mathcal{F}\subseteq T$ (that is, if $F,\,G\in \mathcal{F}$, then there exists $Q\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $\overline{Q}\subseteq F\cap G$) such that for all $i\in \omega$, for all but finitely many $F\in \mathcal{F},\,\overline{F}\subset D_{i}$. Fossy/Morillon [1995]

112. $MC(\infty ,\,LO)$: For every family $X$ of non-empty sets each of which can be linearly ordered there is a function $f$ such that for all $y\in X,\,f(y)$ is a non-empty finite subset of $y$. Howard/Rubin [1977].

126. $MC(\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$, Countable axiom of multiple choice: For every denumerable set $X$ of non-empty sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $y\in X,\,f(y)$ is a non-empty finite subset of $y$. Brunner [1984d] and Blass [1979].

[126 B] Form 131+ form 350. Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

[126 C] $FSCB\ +$ form 131. FSCB is “Every separable first countable space $(X,\,T)$ has a denumerable $\pi$-base.” Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

131. $MC_{\omega }(\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: For every denumerable family $X$ of pairwise disjoint nonempty sets, there is a function $f$ such that for each $x\in X,\,\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is a non-empty countable subset of $x$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin [1997b].

167. $PKW(\aleph _{0},\,\geq 2,\,\infty )$, Partial Kinna-Wagner Principle: For every denumerable family $F$ such that for all $x\in F,\,|x|\geq 2$, there is an infinite subset $H\subseteq F$ and a function $f$ such that for all $x\in H,\,\emptyset \neq f(x)\subsetneq x$. Brunner [1982a].

178($n,\,N$). If $n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2$ and $N\subseteq \{1,2,\,\ldots ,\,n-1\},\, N\neq \emptyset ,\,MC(\infty ,\, n,\,N)$: If $X$ is any set of $n$-element sets then there is a function $f$ with domain $X$ such that for all $A\in X,\,f(A)\subseteq A$ and $|f(A)|\in N$. Zuckerman [1969a], [1981], and note 53.

214. $Z(\omega )$: For every family $A$ of infinite sets, there is a function $f$ such that for all $y\in A,\, f(y)$ is a non-empty subset of $y$ and $|f(y)|=\aleph _{0}$. Pincus [1977a].

218. $(\forall n\in \omega -\{0\})MC$($\infty ,\,\infty$, relatively prime to $n$): $\forall n\in \omega -\{0\}$, if $X$ is a set of non-empty sets, then there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a non-empty, finite subset of $x$ and $|f(x)|$ is relatively prime to $n$. Bleicher [1965].

219. $(\forall n\in \omega \,-\{0\})MC$($\infty ,\,WO$, relatively prime to $n$): For all non-zero $n\in \omega$, if $X$ is a set of non-empty well orderable sets, then there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\, f(x)$ is a non-empty, finite subset of $x$, and $|f(x)|$ is relatively prime to $n$. Pincus [1972a].

292. $MC(LO,\,\infty )$: For each linearly ordered family of non-empty sets $X$, there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in Xf(x)$ is non-empty, finite subset of $x$). Howard/Rubin $[\mathbf{1977}]$.

322. $KW(WO,\,\infty )$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of sets: For every well ordered set $X$ there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in M$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15). Kinna/Wagner [1955], Brunner [1982a].

323. $KW(\infty ,\,WO)$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a family of well orderable sets: For every set $X$ of well orderable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

324. $KW(WO,\,WO)$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of well orderable sets: For every well ordered set $X$ of well orderable sets, there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

327. $KW(WO,\,<\aleph _{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of finite sets: For every well ordered set $X$ of finite sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

328. $MC(WO, \infty )$; For every well ordered set $X$ such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that and for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

329. $MC(\infty , WO)$: For every set $M$ of well orderable sets such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

330. $MC(WO,\,WO)$: For every well ordered set $X$ of well orderable sets such that for all $x\in X,\, |x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin [1997].

333. $MC(\infty ,\,\infty ,\,\mathrm{odd})$: For every set $X$ of sets such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$ and $|f(x)|$ is odd. Keremedis [1996a].

334. $MC$($\infty ,\,\infty$, even): For every set $X$ of sets such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 2$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$ and $|f(x)|$ is even. Keremedis [1996a].

349. $MC(\infty ,\,\aleph _{0})$: For every set $X$ of non-empty denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$.

350. $MC(\aleph _{0},\,\aleph _{0})$: For every denumerable set $X$ of non-empty denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

355. $KW(\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of sets: For every denumerable set $X$ there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

356. $KW(\infty ,\,\aleph _{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a family of denumerable sets: For every set $X$ of denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

357. $KW(\aleph _{0},\,\aleph _{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of denumerable sets: For every denumerable set $X$ of denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

358. $KW(\aleph _{0},\,<\aleph _{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of finite sets: For every denumerable set $X$ of finite sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

376. Restricted Kinna Wagner Principle: For every infinite set $X$ there is an infinite subset $Y$ of $X$ and a function $f$ such that for every $z\subseteq Y$, if $|z|\geq 2$ then $f(z)$ is a non-empty proper subset of $z$. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

IV. Partial Choice $PC$

[1 CC] $PC(\aleph _{0},\,\mathrm{odd},\,\infty ) +MC_{\omega ^{+}}$. $PC(\aleph _{0},\,\mathrm{odd},\,\infty )$ is “Every denumerable family of odd sized (finite) sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function.” and $MC_{\omega ^{+}}$ is “For every natural number $n\geq 1$ and for every set of non-empty sets, there is a function $f$ such that for each $u\in x,\,f(u)$ is a non-empty finite subset of $u$ such that $|f(u)|$ and $n$ are relatively prime.” Note 133.

[8 A] $PC(\infty ,\,\infty ,\,\infty )$: Every infinite family of non-empty sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Brunner [1983b].

[8 B] $PC(\aleph _{0},\,\infty ,\,\infty )$: Every denumerable family of non-empty sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Monro [1975].

[8 S] $PC(WO,\,\infty ,\,\infty )$: Every infinite well ordered set of non-empty sets has an infinite subset with a choice function. $([8\ \mathrm{A}]\rightarrow [8\ \mathrm{S}]\rightarrow [8\ \mathrm{B}])$

[9 T] Restricted Choice: For every infinite set $X$ there is an infinite $Y\subseteq X$ such that the collection of non-empty subsets of $Y$ has a choice function. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

[10 E] $PC(\aleph _{0},\,<\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: Every denumerable family of finite sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Brunner [1983b].

[10 O] $PC(WO,\,<\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: Every infinite well ordered family of finite sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

[18 A] $PC(\aleph _{0},2,\,\infty )$: Every denumerable set of pairs has an infinite subset with a choice function.

[18 C] $PC(WO,\,2,\,\infty )$: Every infinite well ordered set of pairs has an infinite subset with a choice function.

[32 B] $PC(\aleph _{0},\,\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: Every denumerable set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

[32 C] $PC(WO,\,\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: Every infinite well ordered set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

[126 D] For every denumerable family $A$ of disjoint non-empty sets there is an infinite set $C\subset \bigcup A$ such that for every $a\in A,\, 0\leq |C\cap a|<\omega$. Keremedis [1996d] and note 132.

132. $PC(\infty <\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: Every infinite family of finite sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Blass [1977a] and Kleinberg [1969].

150. $PC(\infty ,\,\aleph _{0},\,\infty )$: Every infinite set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

166. $PC(\infty ,\,2,\,\infty )$: Every infinite family of pairs has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Brunner [1982a].

167. $PKW(\aleph _{0},\,\geq 2,\,\infty )$, Partial Kinna-Wagner Principle: For every denumerable family $F$ such that for all $x\in F,\,|x|\geq 2$, there is an infinite subset $H\subseteq F$ and a function $f$ such that for all $x\in H,\,\emptyset \neq f(x)\subsetneq x$. Brunner [1982a].

336($n$). (For $n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2$.) For every infinite set $X$, there is an infinite $Y\subseteq X$ such that the set of all $n$-element subsets of $Y$ has a choice function. Note 111.

342($n$). (For $n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2$.) $PC(\infty ,\,n,\,\infty )$: Every infinite family of $n$-element sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. (See form 166.) Note 111.

373($n$). (For $n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2$.) $PC(\aleph _{0},\,n,\,\infty )$: Every denumerable set of $n$-element sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

[373 A($n$)] (For $n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 2$.) $PC(WO,\,n,\,\infty )$: Every infinite well ordered set of $n$-element sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

378. Restricted Choice for Families of Well Ordered Sets: For every infinite set $X$ there is an infinite subset $Y$ of $X$ such that the family of non-empty well orderable subsets of $Y$ has a choice function. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

[378 A] Restricted Choice for Families of Finite Sets: For every infinite set $X$ there is an infinite subset $Y$ of $X$ such that the family of non-empty finite subsets of $Y$ has a choice function. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

379. $PKW(\infty ,\,\infty ,\,\infty )$: For every infinite family $X$ of sets each of which has at least two elements, there is an infinite subfamily $Y$ of $X$ and a function $f$ such that for all $y\in Y,\,f(y)$ is a non-empty proper subset of $y$. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

380. $PC(\infty ,\,WO,\,\infty )$: For every infinite family of non-empty well orderable sets, there is an infinite subfamily $Y$ of $X$ which has a choice function. De la Cruz/Di Prisco [1996].

V. Conditional Choice Including Variations of Rado’s Lemma

[14 I] Consistency Principle: For every binary mess $M$ on a set $S$ there is a function $f$ on $S$ which is consistent with $M$. Jech [1973b] p 17 and note 109.

[14 O] Let $\{A(i):i\in I\}$ be a collection of finite sets and $R$ a symmetric binary relation on $\bigcup _{i\in I}A(i)$. Suppose that for every finite $W\subseteq I$, there is an $R$-consistent choice function for $\{A(i):i\in W\}$. Then there is an $R$-consistent choice function for $\{A(i):i\in I\}$. Łoś/Ryll-Nardzewski [1951] and note 109.

[14 $\mathbf{P}(n)$] (For $n\geq 3$) [14 O] restricted to $\{A(i):i\in I\}$ such that for all $i\in I,\,|A(i)|\leq n$. Cowen [1977b] and note 109. (For $n=2$ see form 141.)

[14 Y] Form $99$ + form 62. Note 33.

[14 AG] Topological Rado Lemma: Let $\{T_{i}:i\in I\}$ be a family of compact Hausdorff spaces and suppose for each finite $F\subseteq I$, there is a set $\Phi (F)$ of partial choice functions on $I$ whose domains include $F$ and such that (a) $F_{1}\subseteq F_{2}$ implies $\Phi (F_{2})\subseteq \Phi (F_{1})$ and (b) the set $\{\phi |F:\phi \,\in \Phi (F)\}$ is closed in $\prod \{T_{i}:i\in F\}$ in the product topology. Then there is a choice function $f$ on $I$ satisfying for any finite $F\subseteq I,\,\exists \phi \in \Phi (F)$ such that $f$ and $\phi$ coincide on $F$. Rav [1977].

[14 AH] Principle of Consistent Choices: Let $\{T_{i}:i\in I\}$ be a family of compact Hausdorf spaces and suppose $R$ is a symmetric binary relation defined for all pairs of elements belonging to distinct $T_{i}$ and such that for all $i\neq j$ in $I$, the set $E(i,j)=\{(x,\,y):x\,R\,y\ \mathrm{and}\ x\in T_{i}\ \mathrm{and}\ y\in T_{j}\}$ is closed in $T_{i}\times T_{j}$. Furthermore suppose that for every finite subset $F\subseteq I$, with at least two elements, $\exists \phi \in \prod \{T_{i}:i\in F\}$ such that $\phi (i)\,R\,\phi (j)$ for all $i\neq j$ in $F$. Then $\exists f\in \prod \{T_{i}:i\in I\}$ such that $f(i)\,R\,f(j)$ for all $i\neq j$ in $I$. Rav [1977].

[14 AI] Engelers Lemma: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a family of functions whose domains are subsets of a set $S$ with range $\subseteq \{0,1\}$ and such that

(a)

For every finite $F\subseteq S,\,\exists \phi \in \mathcal{E}$ with domain F.

(b)

The restriction of any function in $\mathcal{E}$ to any subset of its domain is in $\mathcal{E}$.

(c)

If $\phi$ is any function with domain $\phi \subseteq S$ such that the restriction of $\phi$ to any finite subset of its domain is in $\mathcal{E}$ then $\phi \in \mathcal{E}$.

Then $\exists f\in \mathcal{E}$ whose domain is $S$. Rav [1977].

[14 AJ] Robinson’s Valuation Lemma: Let $\{\phi _{x}:x\in X\}$ be a family of partial valuations on a set $S$. ($\phi$ is a partial valuation on $S$ if the domain of $\phi \subseteq S$ and the range of $\phi \subseteq \{0,1\}.)$ Suppose $\mathfrak{B}$ is a filter base on $X$ such that for every finite $F\subseteq S$ and for every $B\in \mathfrak{B}$ there is $x\in B$ such that $F\subseteq \ \mathrm{dom}\ \phi _{x}$. Then there is a total valuation $f$ on $S$ (that is, $\mathrm{dom}\,f=S$) such that for all finite $F\subseteq S$ and all $B\in \mathfrak{B},\,\exists x\in B$ such that $F\subseteq \ \mathrm{dom}\,\phi _{x}$ and $f|F=\phi _{x}|F$. ($\mathfrak{B}$ is a filter base means $\forall B_{1},\,B_{2}\in \mathfrak{B},\,\exists B_{3}\in \mathfrak{B}$ such that $B_{3}\subseteq B_{1}\cap B_{2}$.) Rav [1977] and Cowen [1973]. Compare with [14 I].

[14 AK] Let $X$ be a set and $\mathcal{D}=\{Y_{i}:i\in I\}$ a family of finite pairwise disjoint subsets of $\mathcal{P}(X)$. Suppose for every finite subset $\{a,\,b,\,\ldots ,\,k\}$ of $I,\,\exists s\in I$ such that $Y_{s}\subseteq Y_{a}\wedge Y_{b}\wedge \ldots \wedge Y_{k}$ (If $Y$ and $Z$ are finite pairwise disjoint sets then $Y\wedge Z= \{A \cap B:A\in Y\ \mathrm{and}\ B\in Z\ \mathrm{and}\ A \cap B\neq \emptyset \}$.) Then there is a choice function $\mu$ whose domain includes $\mathcal{D}$ such that the family $\{\mu (Y_{i}):i\in I\}$ (where $\mu (Y_{i})\in Y_{i})$ of subsets of $X$ is closed under finite intersections. Rav [1977].

[14 AP] Suppose to each finite subset $F$ of a set I there corresponds a set $\Phi (F)$ of functions whose domains are subsets of $I$ including $F$ and such that (a) $F_{1}\subseteq F_{2}$ implies $\Phi (F_{2})\subseteq \Phi (F_{2})$ and (b) $\forall i\in I,\,\{\phi (i):\phi \in \bigcup \{\Phi (F):F$ finite and $F\subseteq I\}\big \}$ is finite. Then there is a function $f$ with domain $I$ such that for all finite $F\subseteq I,\,\exists \phi \in \Phi (F)$ such that $\phi$ and $f$ coincide on F. Rav [1977], Cowen [1973] and note 80.

[14 AQ] Strong Rado Lemma 1: Let $T$ be a family of finite sets and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of finite subsets of $T$ satisfying

(1)

$(\forall K\in T)(\exists S\in \mathcal{F})(K\in S)$

(2)

$(\forall S_{1},\,S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})(\exists S_{3}\in \mathcal{F})(S_{1}\cup S_{2}\subseteq S_{3})$

Assume there is a function $\phi$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ such that for each $S\in \mathcal{F},\,\phi (S)= \phi _{S}$ is a function with domain $S$ and satisfies $(\forall K\in S)(\phi _{S}(K)\in K)$. Then there is a function $f$ with domain $T$ and with the following property: For all $S\in \mathcal{F}$ there is an $S^{\prime }\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $S\subseteq S^{\prime }$ and $f$ and $\phi _{S^{\prime }}$ agree on $S$. Howard [1993].

[14 AR] Patching Lemma: Let $L$ be a local system of $S$ (that is, $L\subseteq \mathcal{P}(S)$ and for each finite $E\subseteq S$, there exists $H\in L$ such that $E\subseteq H$). Let $F$ be a set and $n$ a positive integer. Suppose that for each $H\in L$, there is a function $f_{H}:H^{n}\rightarrow F$ and $\{f_{H}(x):H\in L\}$ is finite for each $x\in S^{n}$. Then there is a function $f:S^{n}\rightarrow F$ such that for any finite subset $K\subseteq S^{n}$, there is an $H\in L$ with $K\subseteq H^{n}$ and $f$ and $f_{H}$ agree on K. Hickin/Plotkin [1976] and note 83.

[14 AY] Let $F$ be a class of partial functions on $I$ of finite character such that (a) $\{f(\nu ):f \in F\}$ is finite for each $\nu \in I$ and (b) for each finite $W \subseteq I$, there exists $f\in F$ with $\mathrm{dom}(f)=W$. Then $F$ contains a function with domain $I$. ($F$ is of finite character means $f\in F$ iff for all finite $\omega \subseteq I,\,f|w\in F$.) Cowen [1973].

[14 AZ] Let $\Phi =\{\phi _{t}\}_{t\in T}$ be a set of partial valuations on a set $S$ (that is, $\mathrm{dom}(\phi _{t})\subseteq S$ and range$(\phi _{t})\subseteq \{0,1\}$) such that for all finite $U\subseteq S$ there is a $t\in T$ for which $U\subseteq \ \mathrm{dom}(\phi _{t})$. Then there is a valuation $\Psi$ with $\mathrm{dom}(\Psi )=S$ and such that for every finite $U\subseteq S$, there is a $t\in T$ with $U\subseteq \, \mathrm{dom}(\phi _{t})$ and $\Psi |U=\phi _{t}|U$. Cowen [1973].

99. Rado’s Selection Lemma: Let $\{K(\lambda ):\lambda \in \Lambda \}$ be a family of finite subsets (of $X$) and suppose for each finite $S\subseteq \Lambda$ there is a function $\gamma (S):S\rightarrow X$ such that $(\forall \lambda \in S)(\gamma (S)(\lambda )\in K(\lambda ))$. Then there is an $f:\Lambda \rightarrow X$ such that for every finite $S\subseteq \Lambda$ there is a finite $T$ such that $S\subseteq T\subseteq \Lambda$ and such that $f$ and $\gamma (T)$ agree on S. Rado [1949].

[99 A] Weak Rado Lemma: Let $\Lambda$ be a set. Suppose that $\gamma$ is a function with domain all finite subsets of $\Lambda$ such that for each finite $S\subseteq \Lambda ,\,\gamma (S):S\rightarrow \{0,1\}$. Then there is a $\phi$ defined on $\Lambda$ with the property that for every finite $S\subseteq \Lambda$ there is a finite $T\subseteq \Lambda$ such that $S\subseteq T$ and $\gamma (T)$ and $\phi$ agree on $S$. Schechter [1996a] and Howard [1993].

[99 B] Rado’s Lemma restricted to families of two element sets: Let $\{k(\lambda ):\lambda \in \Lambda \}$ be a family of 2 element subsets of a set $X$ and suppose that for each finite $S\subseteq \Lambda$, there is a function $\gamma (S)$ from $S$ into $X$ such that $(\forall \lambda \in S)(\gamma (S)(\lambda )\in k(\lambda ))$. Then there is a function from $\Lambda$ into $X$ such that for every finite $S\subseteq \Lambda$, there is a finite $T$ with $S\subseteq T\subseteq \Lambda$ such that $f$ and $\gamma (T)$ agree on $S$. Rav [1977] and Howard [1993].

[99 C] Strong Rado Lemma 2: Let $T$ be a family of finite sets and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of finite subsets of $T$ satisfying

(1)

$(\forall K\in T)(\exists S\in \mathcal{F})(K\in S)$

(2)

$(\forall S_{1},\,S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})(S_{1}\cup S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})$

Assume there is a function $\phi$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ such that for each $S\in \mathcal{F},\,\phi (S)= \phi _{S}$ is a function with domain $S$ and satisfies $(\forall K\in S)(\phi _{S}(K)\in K)$. Then there is a function $f$ with domain $T$ and with the following property: For all $S\in \mathcal{F}$ there is an $S^{\prime }\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $S\subseteq S^{\prime }$ and $f$ and $\phi _{S^{\prime }}$ agree on $S$. Howard [1993].

107. M. Hall’s Theorem: Let $\{S(\alpha ):\alpha \in A\}$ be a collection of finite subsets (of a set $X$) then if

$$\begin{equation*} {\text{for each finite}}\ F\subseteq A\ {\text{there is an injective choice function on}}\ F \tag{$^{\ast }$} \end{equation*}$$

then there is an injective choice function on $A$. (That is, a 1-1 function $f$ such that $(\forall \alpha \in A)(f(\alpha )\in S(\alpha ))$.) (According to a theorem of P. Hall $(\ast )$ is equivalent to $|\bigcup _{\alpha \in F}S(\alpha )|\geq |F|$. P. Hall’s theorem does not require the axiom of choice.) M. Hall [1948].

141. $[14\mathrm{P}(n)]$ with $n=2$: Let $\{A(i):i\in I\}$ be a collection of sets such that $\forall i\in I,\, |A(i)|\leq 2$ and suppose $R$ is a symmetric binary relation on $\bigcup _{i\in I}A(i)$ such that for all finite $W\subseteq I$ there is an $R$ consistent choice function for $\{A(i):i\in W\}$. Then there is an $R$ consistent choice function for $\{A(i):i\in I\}$. Cowen [1977b] and note 109.

184. Existence of a double uniformization: For all $X$ and $Y$, for all $E\subseteq X\times Y$, if there is an infinite cardinal $\kappa$ satisfying:

(1)

$\forall y_{0}\in Y,\,|\{(x,\,y_{0}):x\in X\}\cap E|=\kappa$ and

(2)

$\forall x_{0}\in X,\,|\{(x_{0},\,y):y\in Y\}\cap E|=\kappa$,

then $\exists U\subseteq E$ such that for all $(x,\,y)\in E,\,\exists !z\in X$ such that $(z,\,y)\in U$ and $\exists !z\in Y$ such that $(x,\,z)\in U$. ($U$ is called a double uniformization of $E$.) Kaniewski/Rogers [1980].

[270 B] $F_{\mathrm{fin}}$: For any family $\mathcal{F}$ of pairwise disjoint, non-empty, finite sets if $R$ is a symmetric binary relation on $\bigcup \mathcal{F}$ which satisfies (i) the set $\{b\in \bigcup \mathcal{F}:\neg a\,R\,b\}$ is finite for every $a\in \bigcup \mathcal{F}$ and (ii) every finite subfamily of $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function, then $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function. Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

[270 $\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{n})$] $F_{n}^{\mathrm{fin}}$ ($n\geq 3$ a natural number): For any family $\mathcal{F}$ of pairwise disjoint, $n$ element sets if $R$ is a symmetric binary relation on $\bigcup \mathcal{F}$ which satisfies (i) the set $\{b\in \bigcup \,\mathcal{F}:\neg a\,R\,b\}$ is finite for every $a\in \bigcup \mathcal{F}$ and (ii) every finite subfamily of $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function, then $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function. Kolany [1992].

VI. Miscellaneous Choice

[14 BW] For every set $E$ there is an ultrafilter choice function on $E$. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

140. Let $\Omega$ be the set of all (undirected) infinite cycles of reals (Graphs whose vertices are real numbers, connected, no loops and each vertex adjacent to exactly two others). Then there is a function $f$ on $\Omega$ such that for all $s\in \Omega ,\,f(s)$ is a direction along $s$. Truss [1984].

[170 A] There is a function that assigns to each denumerable set $D$ of real numbers a real number not in $D$. Sierpiński [1954].

269. For every cardinal $m$, there is a set $A$ such that $2^{|A|^{2}}\geq m$ and there is a choice function on the collection of 2-element subsets of $A$. Lampe [1974].

FIXED POINT THEOREMS

[$\boldsymbol{0}$ J] Zermelo’s Fixed Point Theorem: For every partially ordered set $(X,\,\leq )$, if every well ordered subset has a least upper bound then every $f:X\rightarrow X$ satisfying $\forall t\in X,\,t\leq f(t)$ has a fixed point. Manka [1988a], Zermelo [1908b] and Abian [1980].

[$\boldsymbol{0}$ K] For all partially ordered sets $(X,\,\leq )$, if there is a sup function $\sigma$ on the well ordered subsets of $X$ then every $f:X\rightarrow X$ satisfying $\forall t\in X,\,t\leq f(t)$ has a fixed point. Manka [1988a] and note 38.

[$\boldsymbol{0}$ L] Caristi’s Fixed Point Theorem: If $(X,\,\rho )$ is a complete metric space and $\phi :X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is bounded above and upper semi-continuous then in the Brøndsted ordering $(x\leq y\,\mathrm{iff}\, p(x,\,y)\leq \phi (y)-\phi (x))$ every $f:X\rightarrow X$ satisfying $\forall t\in X,\,t\leq f(t)$ has a fixed point. Caristi [1976], Manka [1988a], and note 38.

[$\boldsymbol{0}$ AI] Turinici’s Fixed Point Theorem for Hausdorff Spaces: If $(X, \leq )$ is a directed, partially ordered set and $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ such that

(a) $(X,\,\leq )$ is upper semi-continuous with respect to $\tau$,

(b) Every well ordered subset of $(X,\,\leq )$ has a unique limit as a net, then every function $f:X\rightarrow X$ such that $\forall x\in X,\,x\leq f(x)$ has a fixed point. Manka [1988b] and note 38.

[1 V] For every partially ordered set $(X,\,\leq )$, if every well ordered subset is bounded above then every function $f:X\rightarrow X$ satisfying $\forall t\in X,\,t\leq f(t)$ has a fixed point. Manka [1988a] and Abian [1980].

[1 AJ] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of mappings of a poset $(X,\,\leq )$ into itself such that $\forall f\in \mathcal{F},\,\forall x\in X,\,f(x)\leq x$. If for some element $e$ of $X$ each chain in $X$ containing $e$ has a lower bound, then the family $\mathcal{F}$ has a common fixed point. Kasahara [1976].

[1 AS] Turinici’s Fixed Point Theorem: If $(X,\,\leq )$ is a directed, partially ordered set and $\tau$ is a topology on $X$ such that

(a) $(X,\,\leq )$ is upper semicontinuous with respect to $\tau$,

(b) Every well ordered subset of $(X,\,\leq )$ is convergent as a net, then every function $f:X\rightarrow X$ such that $\forall x\in X,\,x\leq f(x)$ has a fixed point. Manka [1988b] and note 38.

[1 BC] Assume $P$ is a partially ordered set in which every non-empty chain has an upper bound and $f:P\rightarrow P$ satisfies $\forall x\in f(P)\cup \{a\in P: a\ {\text{is an upper bound for some chain in}}\ f(P)\},\, x\leq f(f(x))$. Then $f$ has a fixed apex $u$ (that is, there is some $v\in P$ such that $f(u)=v$ and $f(v)=u$.). Tasković [1988], [1992a].

[1 BD] Let $P$ be a partially ordered set in which every increasing sequence has an upper bound and $f:P\rightarrow P$ satisfies $x\leq f(f(x))$ for all $x\in f(P)\cup \{x\in P:x$ is an upper bound for some increasing sequence in $f(P)\}$. Then $f$ has a fixed apex $u$ (that is, $\exists v\in P$, such that $f(u)=v$ and $f(v) =u$). (For purposes of [1 BD], “sequence” means a function whose domain is an ordinal.) Tasković [1992b].

285. Let $E$ be a set and $f:E\rightarrow E$, then $f$ has a fixed point if and only if $E$ is not the union of three mutually disjoint sets $E_{1},\,E_{2}$ and $E_{3}$ such that $E_{i}\cap f(E_{i})=\emptyset$ for $i=1,2,3$. Makowski/Wiśniewski [1969], Abian [1968], Baker [1964], and Kenyon [1963].

316. If a linearly ordered set $(A,\,\leq )$ has the fixed point property then $(A,\,\leq )$ is complete. ($(A,\,\leq )$ has the fixed point property if every function $f:A\rightarrow A$ satisfying $(x\leq y\Rightarrow f(x)\leq f(y)$) has a fixed point, and ($(A,\,\leq )$ is complete if every subset of $A$ has a least upper bound.) Höft/Howard [1994].

GRAPH THEORETIC FORMS

[1 AT] For all cardinal numbers $\kappa _{1}$ and $\kappa _{2}$, if a graph is both $\kappa _{1}$ and $\kappa _{2}$ colorable then it is also $\kappa$ colorable for some $\kappa$ such that $\kappa \leq ^{\ast }\kappa _{1}$ and $\kappa \leq ^{\ast }n_{2}$. ($\leq ^{\ast }$ is the surjective cardinal ordering). Galvin/Komjáth [1991] and note 118.

[1 AU] Every graph has an irreducible, good coloring. Galvin/Komjáth [1991] and note 118.

[1 AV] Every graph of the form $G(A,\,H(A))$ has an irreducible, good coloring. ($H$ is the Hartogs aleph function.) Galvin/Komjáth [1991] and note 118.

[1 AW] Every graph has a chromatic number. Galvin/Komjáth [1991] and note 118.

[14 $\mathbf{G}(\mathbf{n})$] $(n\in \omega ,\,n\geq 3)\,P_{n}$: For every graph $G$ if every finite subgraph of $G$ is $n$-colorable then $G$ is $n$-colorable. Läuchli [1971] and note 117.

[14 M] R. Cowen’s Generalization of Konig’s Lemma: Let $T$ be a collection of locally finite trees such that for any finite set of levels of $T$, there is a consistent set of vertices piercing those levels. Then there is a consistent set of vertices piercing the entire set of levels of T. Cowen [1977b] and note 21.

[14 $\mathbf{N}(\mathbf{n})$] $(n\in \omega ,\, n\geq 2)$ [14 M] restricted to families of trees where no tree in the family has a vertex with more than $n$ successors. Cowen [1977b], Howard [1984a], and note 21.

[14 BD] Let $H$ be a hypergraph. If every finite subhypergraph has an independent vertex cover then $H$ has an independent vertex cover. Cowen [1990] and note 117.

[14 BE] Let $H$ be a hypergraph. If every finite subhypergraph is 2-colorable then $H$ is 2-colorable. Cowen [1990] and note 117.

[14 BF] Let $H$ be a hypergraph whose edges contain at most three vertices. If every finite subhypergraph of $H$ has an independent vertex cover then $H$ has an independent vertex cover. Cowen [1990] and note 117.

[14 BG] Let $H$ be a hypergraph whose edges contain at most three vertices. If every finite subhypergraph of $H$ is 2-colorable then $H$ is 2-colorable. Cowen [1990] and note 117.

[88 B] $G_{2}$: A graph is 2-colorable if every finite subgraph is 2-colorable. Mycielski [1961] and note 117.

LOGIC (FORMS FROM LOGIC)

[$\boldsymbol{0}$ AA] $CT_{1}$: Restricted Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic I: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable and if each propositional variable occurs in at most one formula in $\Sigma$, then $\Sigma$ is satisfiable. Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

[10 J] Let $S$ be a denumerable set of propositional sentences over an infinite set of propositional letters (in a propositional language where conjunction and disjunction are operators on unordered finite sets of sentences). Then $S$ has a model if and only if every finite subset of $S$ has a model. Lolli [1977].

[10 K] Let $S$ be a consistent denumerable set of sentences in a first order language (where conjunction and disjunction are operators on unordered finite sets of sentences). Then $S$ has a model. Note 19.

[10 L] Let $S$ be a denumerable set of sentences in a first order language (where conjunction and disjunction are operators on unordered finite sets of sentences) such that every finite subset has a model. Then $S$ has a model. Note 19.

[14 H] Compactness Theorem for First Order Logic: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a first order language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ has a model then $\Sigma$ has a model. Henkin [1954a] and Jech [1973b] p 17.

[14 AW] The Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable, then $\Sigma$ is satisfiable. Henkin [1954b].

[14 AX] Structural Completeness Theorem for Propositional Logic: Assume At is a set of propositional variables and $S$ is the set of propositional formulas generated by At. Assume $X \subseteq S$ and $a\in S$ satisfy the following: For any function $e : At \rightarrow S$ if $Cn(\{b[e] : b \in X\}) \subseteq \ Cn(\emptyset )$ then $a[e] \in Cn(\emptyset )$. Then $a\in Cn(X)$. ($Cn(Y)$ is the deductive closure of $Y\cup$ all substitutions of axioms for the classical predicate calculus and for $a\in S,\, a[e]$ is $a$ with each propositional variable $p$ replaced by $e(p)$.) Pogorzelski/Prucnal [1974].

[14 CI] 3-Sat: Restricted Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic II: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable and if every formula in $\Sigma$ is a disjunction of at most three literals, then $\Sigma$ is satisfiable. (A literal is a propositional variable or its negation.) Cowen [1990].

[14 CJ] The Completeness Theorem for Propositional Logic: Every consistent set of formulas is satisfiable. Henkin [1954a] and [1954b].

[14 CK] The Completeness Theorem for First Order Logic: Every consistent set of formulas is satisfiable. Henkin [1954a] and [1954b].

42. Löwenheim-Skolem Theorem: If a countable family of first order sentences is satisfiable in a set $M$ then it is satisfiable in a countable subset of $M$. G. Moore [1982] p 251.

[43 B] Countable Henkin Principle: Let $\Phi$ be the class of formulas in a language that includes the language of the sentential calculus. Let $I$ be a countable set of inferences, and $\Gamma$ a consistent subset of $\Phi$ such that $\Gamma \cup \{\psi \}$ respects $I$ for each $\psi \in \Phi$. Then for any $\phi \in \Phi$, if $\phi$ is consistent with $\Gamma$ then $\Gamma$ has a finitely consistent extension that contains $\phi$ and decides $I$. Goldblatt [1985] and note.

[43 P] The ultraproduct of a well founded structure by a countably complete ultrafilter is well founded. Spector [1980] and note 54.

253. Loś’ Theorem: If $M = \langle A,R_{j}\rangle _{j\in J}$ is a relational system, $X$ any set and $\mathcal{F}$ an ultrafilter in $\mathcal{P}(X)$ then $M$ and $M^{X}/\mathcal{F}$ are elementarily equivalent. Howard [1975].

270. $CT_{\mathrm{fin}}$: The compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs only in a finite number of formulas. Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

[270 A] $C(\infty , < \aleph _{0})\wedge CT_{2}$ ($CT_{2}$ is the compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs in at most two formulas. See form 271($n$).) Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

271 ($n$). If $n\in \omega -\{0,1\}, CT_{n}$: The compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs in at most $n$ formulas. Kolany/Wojtylak [1991].

326. 2-SAT: Restricted Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic III: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable and if every formula in $\Sigma$ is a disjunction of at most two literals, then $\Sigma$ is satisfiable. (A literal is a propositional variable or its negation.) Wojtylak [1995].

MAXIMAL PRINCIPLES

[1 B] Every commutative ring with unit has a maximal ideal. Hodges [1979].

[1 M] The ramification Lemma: If $S: X^{\leq \theta }\rightarrow \mathcal{P}(E)$ is a ramification system, then for each $g\in E$ there is an $f$ which is maximal (with respect to inclusion) in $\{h\in X^{\leq \theta } : g\in S(h)\}$. Brunner [1989] and note 22.

[1 AN] Every lattice $\langle L,\cap ,\cup ,\subseteq \rangle$ of sets (that is, $L$ is a family of sets and $\cap ,\,\cup$ and $\subseteq$ are the usual operations) with a greatest element has a maximal, proper ideal. Bell/Fremlin [1972].

[1 BA] (Depends on the prime $p$) Every group has a maximal $p$-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[1 BI] $(\mathrm{M}T_{0})$: Every topological space has a maximal $T_{0}$ subspace. Schnare [1968] and note 106.

[1 BO] For every $T_{1}$ topological space $(X,\,T)$ and every base (subbase) $B$ for $X$ there exists a $\subseteq$-maximal cellular family $Q\subseteq B$. Keremedis [1996b] and note 77.

[1 BT] For every Boolean ring $(B,+,\cdot )$ and every $H\subseteq B$ which is closed under + there exists a $\subseteq$-maximal ideal $Q\subseteq B$ such that $H\cap Q = \{0\}$. Keremedis [1996c].

[1 CD] In a commutative ring, every proper ideal can be extended to a maximal ideal. Krull [1929]. ([1 CD] implies [1 B]).

[14 A] Ultrafilter Theorem: Every proper filter over a set $S$ (in $\mathcal{P}(S)$) can be extended to an ultrafilter. Jech [1973b] p 17.

[14 E] Almost Maximal Ideal Theorem: Every bounded, non-trivial, distributive lattice has an almost maximal ideal. (Definitions: If $D$ is a bounded non-trivial distributive lattice, $I(D)$ is the lattice of ideals of $D$. An almost maximal ideal in $D$ is an ideal $P$ of $D$ such that $s(P) = P$ where s is the operation on $I(D)$ defined as follows: If $e$ is the unit of $I(D)$, (i) For $a \in I(D)$ we say $x \in I(D)$ is a-small if $x \vee b = e$ implies $a \vee b = e$ for all $b \in I(D)$. (ii) For any $a\in I(D), s(a)$ is the join of all a-small elements of $I(D)$). Banaschewski/Harting [1985] and Blass [1986].

[14 T] Every regular commutative ring with unit has a maximal ideal. Banaschewski [1983] and note 29.

[14 U] Every closed proper ideal in a Gelfand algebra is contained in some maximal ideal. Banaschewski [1983] and note 29.

[14 V] FIP Extension Principle: Let $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{X}$ have the finite intersection property, then $\mathcal{F}\subseteq U$ for some ultrafilter $U$ on $X$. Schechter [1996a].

[14 BV] For every set $E$ there is an effectively $E$-adequate ultrafilter. Morillon [1988], [1985] and note 71.

[14 BW] For every set $E$ there is an ultrafilter choice function on $E$. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

[14 BX] If $(E_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of sets and $(F_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family such that for each $i, F_{i}$ is a filter in $\mathcal{P}(E_{i})$ then there is a family $(U_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that for each $i\in I,\,U_{i}$ is an ultrafilter in $\mathcal{P}(E_{i})$ containing $F_{i}$. Morillon [1985], [1988] and note 71.

[14 BY] For every topological space X, every proper ideal in the normed $\mathbb{R}$-algebra of continuous bounded functions from $X$ into $\mathbb{R}$ is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon [1988].

[14 BZ] Every proper ideal in a non-trivial normed $\mathbb{R}$-algebra or $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with identity is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon [1988].

[14 CA] If $(A_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of non trivial commutative normed algebras with identity then there is a family $(J_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that for each $i\in I, J_{i}$ is a maximal ideal in $A_{i}$. Morillon [1988].

[14 CB] If $X$ is a topological space and $I$ is a proper ideal in the algebra of all bounded continuous functions from $X$ to $\mathbb{R}$ such that every function in $I$ vanishes at at least one point of $X$ then $I$ is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon [1988].

[30 G] Weak Hausdorff Lemma: For every set $X$, every $\subseteq$-chain in $\mathcal{P}(X)$ is contained in a maximal $\subseteq$-chain. Note 130.

[43 L] $Z_{\omega }$: If every chain in a partially ordered set $P$ is finite, then $P$ contains a maximal element. Tarski [1948], Wolk [1983], and note 54.

[43 M] If $(X, \rho )$ is a complete metric space and $\phi : X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is bounded above and upper semi-continuous then in the Brøndsted ordering, $(x < y\ \mathrm{iff}\ \rho (x, y)\leq \phi (y)-\phi (x))$, there is a maximal element. Brunner [1987a] and note 38.

[50 I] If $A$ is a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra $B$, then there is a $\subseteq$-maximal proper filter $F$ in $B$ such that $F\cap A =\{1\}$. Bell [1988]

[51 B] $Z(L,\,W)$: Every non-empty linearly ordered set in which every well ordered subset has an upper bound has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976], Manka [1988a], H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985] p 37 $M1(L,\,W)$, and note 39.

[62 C] For every prime $p$, if $\{G_{y}: y\in Y\}$ is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product $\prod _{y \in Y} G_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[62 D] For every prime $p$, if $Y$ is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product $\prod _{y\in Y} S_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. ($S_{y}$ is the symmetric group on $y$.) Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

63. $SPI$: Weak ultrafilter principle: Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter. Jech [1973b] p 172 prob 8.5.

70. There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$. Jech [1973b] prob 5.24.

[70 A] Every Dedekind infinite set has a non-principal ultrafilter.

[87 A($\alpha$)] $Z_{\aleph _{\alpha }}$: Let $P$ be a partially ordered set in which every well ordered chain has type $<\aleph _{\alpha }$. If every well ordered chain in $P$ has an upper bound in $P$, then $P$ contains a maximal element. Wolk [1983].

[87 B($\alpha$)] $Z_{\aleph _{\alpha }}^{\ast }$: Let $P$ be a well-founded partially ordered set (that is, every chain in $P$ is well ordered.) in which every chain has type $<\aleph _{\alpha }$. If every chain in $P$ has an upper bound in $P$, then $P$ contains a maximal element. Wolk [1983].

89. Antichain Principle: Every partially ordered set has a maximal antichain. Jech [1973b] p 133 and Kurepa [1953].

[89 A] If $\forall y\in X, y = \langle u,R\rangle$ where $R$ is a partial order on $u$ then there is a function $f$ on $X$ such that $\forall \langle u, R\rangle \in X, f(\langle u,R\rangle )$ is a maximal antichain in $u$. Felgner [1969] and Harper/Rubin [1976].

123. $SPI^{\ast }$: Uniform weak ultrafilter principle: For each family $F$ of infinite sets $\exists f$ such that $\forall x \in F, f(x)$ is a non-principal ultrafilter on $x$. Halpern [1972]

143. $H(C,TR)$: If $(X,\,R)$ is a connected relation$(u\neq v\rightarrow u\,R\,v\ \mathrm{or}\ v\,R\,u)$ then $X$ contains a $\subseteq$-maximal transitive subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

201. Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Every Boolean algebra has a maximal linked system. ($L \subseteq B$ is linked if $a \wedge b\neq 0$ for all $a$ and $b\in L$.) Schrijver [1978].

[201 A] Strong Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Each linked system in a Boolean algebra is contained in some maximal linked system. (If $B$ is a Boolean algebra, $L\subseteq B$ is linked if $a\wedge b\neq 0$ for all $a$ and $b\in L$.) Schrijver [1978].

[202 A] $H(TR\&C,P)$: If $(X,\,R)$ is a transitive, connected relation. Then $X$ has a $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

206. The existence of a non-principal ultrafilter: There exists an infinite set $X$ and a non-principal ultrafilter on $X$. Blass [1977b].

225. Every proper filter on $\omega$ can be extended to an ultrafilter. Rav [1977].

244. Every principal ideal domain has a maximal ideal. Hodges [1976a] and note 84.

254. $Z(D, P, l)$: Every directed relation $(P, R)$ in which ramified subsets have least upper bounds, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

255. $Z(D, R)$: Every directed relation $(P,\,R)$ in which every ramified subset $A$ has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

256. $Z(P,F)$: Every partially ordered set $(X,\,R)$ in which every forest $A$ has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

257. $Z(TR,\,P)$: Every transitive relation $(X,\,R)$ in which every partially ordered subset has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

258. $Z(D,\,L)$: Every directed relation $(X,\,R)$ in which linearly ordered subsets have upper bounds, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

259. $Z(TR\&C, W)$: If $(X,\,R)$ is a transitive and connected relation in which every well ordered subset has an upper bound, then $(X,\,R)$ has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

260. $Z(TR\&C,P)$: If $(X,\,R)$ is a transitive and connected relation in which every partially ordered subset has an upper bound, then $(X,\,R)$ has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

261. $Z(TR,\,T)$: Every transitive relation $(X,\,R)$ in which every subset which is a tree has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

262. $Z(TR,\,R)$: Every transitive relation $(X, R)$ in which every ramified subset $A$ has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

263. $H(AS\&C,P)$: Every every relation $(X,\,R)$ which is antisymmetric and connected contains a $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

264. $H(C, P)$: Every connected relation $(X,\,R)$ contains a $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered set. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

265. $H(A,\,TR)$: Every relation $(X,\,R)$ contains a $\subseteq$-maximal transitive subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

266. $H(AS,\,P)$: Every antisymmetric relation contains $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin [1976] and note 39.

278. In an integral domain $R$, if every ideal is finitely generated then $R$ has a maximal proper ideal. Hodges [1974] and note 45 E.

289. If $S$ is a set of subsets of a countable set and $S$ is closed under chain unions, then $S$ has a $\subseteq$-maximal element. Smullyan [1994] and note 102.

303. If $B$ is a Boolean algebra, $S\subseteq B$ and $S$ is closed under $\wedge$, then there is a $\subseteq$-maximal proper ideal $I$ of $B$ such that $I \cap S =\{0\}$. H. Rubin/J. Rubin [1985].

308($p$). If $p$ is a prime and if $\{G_{y}:y\in Y\}$ is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product $\prod _{y\in Y}G_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[308 A($p$)] If $p$ is a prime and if $Y$ is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product $\prod _{y\in Y}S_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. $(S_{y}$ is the symmetric group on $y$.) Howard/Yorke [1987] and note 24.

[317 A] If $B$ is a complete, well orderable Boolean algebra and $A$ is a Boolean algebra of which $B$ is a subalgebra, then there is an ideal $I$ of $A$ satisfying $I\cap B =\{0\}$ and $I$ is maximal among those ideals $J$ of $A$ satisfying $J\cap B=\{0\}$. Howard [1973].

345. Rasiowa-Sikorski Axiom: If $(B,\,\wedge ,\,\vee )$ is a Boolean algebra, $a$ is a non-zero element of $B$, and $\{X_{n}:n\in \omega \}$ is a denumerable set of subsets of $B$ then there is a maximal prime filter $F$ of $B$ such that $a\in F$ and for each $n\in \omega$, if $X_{n}\subseteq F$ and $\bigwedge X_{n}$ exists then $\bigwedge X_{n}\in F$. Morillon [1988].

MEASURES (FORMS INVOLVING MEASURES ON SETS)

[14 AV] Every Boolean algebra has a 2-valued measure. Pincus [1972c] and note 147.

[14 BC] If $m_{0}$ is an additive, real valued measure on a subalgebra $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{B}$ then there exists a measure $m$ on $\mathcal{B}$ such that $m=m_{0}$ on $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ and the range of $m$ is contained in the closure of the range of $m_{0}$. Tarski [1930] and note 147.

37. Lebesgue measure is countably additive. Sierpiński [1916].

[52 A] On every Boolean algebra there is an additive real valued measure. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 B] For every proper filter $\mathcal{F}$ of elements of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{B}$, there exists an additive, real valued measure $m$ on $\mathcal{B}$ such that $m(x)=1$ for all $x\in \mathcal{F}$. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 C] For every non-empty set X and every proper ideal $\mathcal{I}$ of in $\mathcal{P}(X)$ there is a measure $m$ on $\mathcal{P}(X)$ such that $m(x)=0$ for all $x\in \mathcal{I}$. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[52 D] Let $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ be a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{B}$ and $m_{0}$ an additive, real valued measure on $\mathcal{B}_{0}$. Then there is a real valued, additive measure $m$ on $\mathcal{B}$ such that $m=m_{0}$ on $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ and the range of $m$ is contained in the closed convex hull of the range of $m_{0}$. Luxemburg [1969] and note 147.

[70 C] There is a 2-valued measure on $\mathcal{P}(\omega )$. Pincus [1972c] and note 147.

93. There is a non-measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}$. Sierpiński [1918].

221. For all infinite $X$, there is a non-principal measure on $\mathcal{P}(X)$. Pincus/Solovay [1977] and note 147.

222. There is a non-principal measure on $\mathcal{P}(\omega )$. Pincus/Solovay [1977] and note 147.

223. There is an infinite set $X$ and a non-principal measure on $\mathcal{P}(X)$. Pincus/Solovay [1977] and note 147.

310. The Measure Extension Theorem: Suppose that $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ is a subring (that is, $a,\,b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}\rightarrow a\vee b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}$ and $a-b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}$) of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mu$ is a measure on $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ (that is, $\mu \,:\,\mathcal{A}\rightarrow [0,\,\infty ],\,\mu (a\vee b)=\mu (a)+\mu (b)$ for $a\wedge b=0$, and $\mu (0)=0$.) then there is a measure on $\mathcal{A}$ that extends $\mu$. Wagon [1985].

311. Abelian groups are amenable. ($G$ is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{P}(G)$ such that $\mu (G)=1$ and $\forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A)$.) Wagon bib:1985u.

312. A subgroup of an amenable group is amenable. ($G$ is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{P}(G)$ such that $\mu (G)=1$ and $\forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A)$.) Wagon [1985].

313. $\mathbb{Z}$ (the set of integers under addition) is amenable. ($G$ is amenable if there is a finitely additive measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{P}(G)$ such that $\mu (G)=1$ and $\forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu (gA)=\mu (A)$.) Wagon [1985].

[370 A] Measured Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem: If $\mathcal{B}$ is a Boolean algebra and there is a measure on $\mathcal{B}$ then there is an ultrafilter on $\mathcal{B}$. Morillon [1989], [1990] and note 147.
